finding.claim: The /admin/users/<uid>/ban route catches the admin-check failure and still performs the ban, so any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user.
finding.source: Any caller of POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban; uid comes from the URL path (admin.py:15). Precondition: g.user is a dict-like object, so the except handler at line 19 does not itself raise. The caller needs no admin role.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a protected admin operation, reached unconditionally after the authorization check fails.

trace.note: Route registered for POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with no decorator-level auth guard.
require_admin(g.user) runs inside try. For a non-admin user, user.get('is_admin') is falsy, so abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden.
except Exception catches the Forbidden, which is an Exception subclass, so the 403 is swallowed.
Logs a warning and falls through. The handler does not return or re-raise.
do_ban(uid) executes for the non-admin caller.
Returns {ok: true}, so the caller sees success.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin raises abort(403) on non-admin users (admin.py:10-11), but the caller catches the exception with a broad except and does not return or re-raise (admin.py:16-20). The unban route at admin.py:24-28 calls require_admin without try/except and is correct, which shows the ban route's guard was meant to stop the request. No decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint-level guard is visible in this repo, so g.user population and any upstream auth middleware could not be inspected. do_ban/do_unban are stubs here (admin.py:31-36), so the concrete impact depends on the real implementations, which are not in this repo. If g.user is unset, line 19 raises AttributeError and the ban does not run, so the attack needs an authenticated session or an anonymous user dict.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 calls abort(403) on non-admin users, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try, and the broad `except Exception` at admin.py:18 catches the werkzeug Forbidden. The handler at admin.py:19 only logs and falls through, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs and jsonify(ok=True) returns at admin.py:21. The unban route at admin.py:26 calls require_admin with no try, so it is correctly guarded. No decorator, before_request hook, or blueprint guard appears in the repo; upstream middleware that populates g.user could not be inspected.
verdict.reason: admin.py:17-20 wraps require_admin in a broad except that logs at line 19 and falls through to do_ban(uid) at line 20, so a non-admin caller who gets the 403 from admin.py:11 still performs the ban and receives ok=true. The trace matches the code, and no effective guard exists in this repo; the real-world impact depends on the do_ban stub at admin.py:31-32, which is not implemented here.
